questions.q: Where do you create a new RLS role in Power BI Desktop?
options: File → Publish → Manage Roles
It can only be created in the Power BI service, never Desktop
Home tab → Refresh → Manage Roles
Modeling tab → Manage Roles → New
questions.explain: Roles are defined in Desktop via the Modeling tab's Manage Roles dialog, where selecting New starts a new role definition.

questions.q: What can you NOT do from inside Desktop's Manage Roles dialog?
options: Write a DAX filter expression
Assign users to the role — that only happens in the Power BI service after publishing
Select which table to filter
Name the role
questions.explain: Desktop lets you define the role and its filter, but user assignment is exclusively a service-side step, covered in Lesson 81.

questions.q: When must you switch from the default editor to the DAX editor when defining a role's filter?
options: Never — the DAX editor is deprecated
When the filter needs a dynamic DAX function like USERNAME() or USERPRINCIPALNAME(), which the default drop-down editor can't express
Only when filtering a table with more than 1000 rows
Every single time, regardless of the filter
questions.explain: The default editor only handles simple static filters. Dynamic expressions using DAX functions require switching to the DAX editor.

questions.q: What does the DAX filter expression [Region] = "West" do when applied as an RLS role filter?
options: It renames the Region column to 'West' for all users
It deletes every row where Region does not equal 'West' from the underlying data source
It applies only to the report's visuals, not the underlying semantic model
It evaluates TRUE/FALSE per row, keeping only rows where Region equals 'West' visible to anyone assigned to that role
questions.explain: An RLS filter expression is evaluated per row; only rows returning TRUE remain visible to a user assigned to that role — the underlying data source itself is untouched.

questions.q: Why can't you name an RLS role 'London,Paris'?
options: There's actually no restriction on role names at all
Role names must be exactly one word
Role names can't contain any letters
Role names can't contain a comma
questions.explain: Power BI explicitly disallows commas in role names — a small but real constraint worth knowing before you hit the error.
